# Nova API — /api/pipelines

The operations Nova tags `public` under `/api/pipelines`. Generated from `reference-src/nova-openapi.json`.

## GET /api/pipelines

Operation id `pipelines_list`: in Python `client.call("pipelines_list", …)`, on the command line `stardelt api pipelines_list`.

The pipelines the caller may see: their groups' pipelines, and every pipeline for an administrator. A pipeline without `spec.ownerGroup` is administrators-only. `state` is one of `loading`, `paused`, `running`, `failed`, `succeeded`, `idle`; `loaded` is false while Airflow has no DAG for a new pipeline yet. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

**Responses**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | The visible pipelines, sorted by name |
| `401` | No token to sign in with |
| `502` | The scheduler or the cluster did not answer |
| `503` | No cluster connection, or the scheduler is not configured |

## POST /api/pipelines

Operation id `pipelines_create`: in Python `client.call("pipelines_create", …)`, on the command line `stardelt api pipelines_create`.

Schedule a statement or a published notebook: create a `Pipeline` for one of the caller's owner groups (`runAs: pipeline-<group>`), validated so the loader accepts it. A body gives exactly one of a non-empty `sql` and a `notebook` (`{ name, objectVersion, params }`) — both or neither is 400 `give a statement, a notebook, a dbt run or a quality run`. A body may instead give `tasks` (`[{ name, sql | notebook | dbt | quality, dependsOn }]`, 1 to 30 tasks, each with exactly one source, at most 8 dependencies): `tasks` together with `sql` or `notebook` is 400 `give a statement, a notebook or a task list`; a task name outside `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$`, a name used twice, more than 30 tasks, a dependency on itself or on a task of another pipeline, and a cycle are 400 with a sentence that names the task. Refusals, in this order: a name outside 1 to 40 lower-case letters, digits and dashes starting with a letter 400; a group the caller is not a member of 403 (`you are not a member of the group <g>` — administrators included); a group without a ready `ServicePrincipal` 409 with the `principals` route's message; an empty, over-20,000-character or NUL-carrying statement 400; a parameter name, a parameter count or value, or a `${…}` placeholder the loader cannot fill 400; a notebook name outside `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._ -]{0,127}\.ipynb$` 400, more than 32 notebook parameters, a value over 256 characters or NUL, or a `params` JSON text over 4096 characters 400, and a version that is not in the store 400 `that notebook version does not exist in group <g>` (503 when `NOVA_S3_*` is unset, 502 when S3 does not answer); a retry, wait, time-limit or run-mode option out of range 400; a cron that is not five in-range fields or fires more often than every five minutes 400; an unknown IANA timezone 400; a name that already exists 409; more than ten creations per user per hour 429. `options` and `params` are optional: an omitted option keeps its default (1 retry after 5 minutes, a 120-minute time limit, `Forbid`); `params` are the statement's `${params.<name>}` values, a notebook's values are in `notebook.params`. Airflow is not needed: the resource is the source of truth, and the answer is the new pipeline with `loaded: false`, `state: "loading"`. In a stage whose NOVA_STAGE_KIND is prod, a body that schedules a notebook is refused with 400 "In production a notebook comes from Git. Deploy it with a bundle." unless it carries a bundle deploy stamp (provenance, or one already on the pipeline); other stages and statement schedules are unaffected. The audit line carries the statement's length, the cron and, for a notebook, the group, the file name and the pinned version — never the statement and never a parameter value. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

## POST /api/pipelines/check

Operation id `pipelines_check`: in Python `client.call("pipelines_check", …)`, on the command line `stardelt api pipelines_check`.

What the engine says about a statement, without running it: Nova fills the statement's `${run.date}` (today, UTC), `${run.id}` (`check`) and `${params.<name>}` placeholders and sends `EXPLAIN <statement>` to the engine as the caller, under the source `nova-schedule-check`. It never sends `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` and never the statement itself. `checked: false` means this kind of statement cannot be checked here (only `select`, `with`, `insert`, `merge`, `delete`, `update`, `values` and `create … as …` are). A refused statement answers 200 with `ok: false` and the engine's sentence; an engine that does not answer is 502. Refusals before the engine: an empty, over-20,000-character or NUL-carrying statement 400, a parameter table or a placeholder as on create 400. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

**Request body**

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `params` | object (map of string) | No |  | The parameters the statement's `${params.<name>}` placeholders are filled with. |  |
| `sql` | string | Yes |  |  |  |

**Responses**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | The engine's verdict, or that this statement cannot be checked |
| `400` | The statement, a parameter or a placeholder is invalid |
| `401` | No token to sign in with |
| `502` | The query engine is not reachable |

## POST /api/pipelines/preview-schedule

Operation id `pipelines_preview_schedule`: in Python `client.call("pipelines_preview_schedule", …)`, on the command line `stardelt api pipelines_preview_schedule`.

The next fire times of a cron in its zone, RFC 3339 with that zone's offset (for example `2026-10-21T03:00:00+02:00`), so the Schedule dialog can show what a cadence means before it is saved. A field or a zone as on create (400 with the same sentences); `count` is 1 to 10, 5 when omitted. Like croniter, a day matches when both day fields are restricted and either matches, and when one is unrestricted and the other matches. A wall-clock time the zone skips at a DST jump is not a run; a time that happens twice is answered with its first occurrence. A cron that can never fire answers fewer runs (at most 366 days are searched), not an error. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

**Request body**

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | integer (nullable) | No |  | How many runs to list, 1 to 10; 5 when omitted. | min 0 |
| `cron` | string | Yes |  |  |  |
| `timezone` | string | Yes |  |  |  |

**Responses**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | The next runs in the schedule's zone |
| `400` | The cron, the timezone or the count is invalid |
| `401` | No token to sign in with |

## GET /api/pipelines/principals

Operation id `pipelines_principals`: in Python `client.call("pipelines_principals", …)`, on the command line `stardelt api pipelines_principals`.

The caller's own groups and the pipeline principal of each. `principal` is `pipeline-<group>` when a `ServicePrincipal` of that name with `spec.ownerGroup` equal to the group exists; `ready` is its `status.ready`. `message` is `null` when it is ready, otherwise the `Ready` condition's message (or `no status yet`), and for a group without a principal the `ServicePrincipal` to apply (on a `make install` platform, the `make sync-principal NAME=pipeline-<group> GROUP=<group>` command). A group without a ready principal cannot schedule. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

**Responses**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | One entry per group of the caller, sorted by group |
| `401` | No token to sign in with |
| `502` | The cluster did not answer |
| `503` | No cluster connection |

## POST /api/pipelines/validate

Operation id `pipelines_validate`: in Python `client.call("pipelines_validate", …)`, on the command line `stardelt api pipelines_validate`.

Check a pipeline document without writing it: the body is the body of `pipelines_create` (the document `stardelt apply` reads). It runs every rule a create runs (the name, the caller's own group, the group's ready principal, exactly one of a statement and a notebook with the rules of its kind, the options, the schedule) and then looks at the name: free means `create`; a pipeline Nova wrote that the caller may act on, in the same group, means `update`; a pipeline written outside Nova, someone else's, or in another group is a problem. A body may instead give `tasks` (`[{ name, sql | notebook, dependsOn }]`, 1 to 30 tasks, each with exactly one of the two, at most 8 dependencies): `tasks` together with `sql` or `notebook` is 400 `give a statement, a notebook or a task list`; a task name outside `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$`, a name used twice, more than 30 tasks, a dependency on itself or on a task of another pipeline, and a cycle are 400 with a sentence that names the task. A rule that refuses is an answer, `ok: false` with one sentence in `errors`, status 200; nothing is written and no creation slot is taken. An accepted document with a schedule lists its next five fire times. In a stage whose NOVA_STAGE_KIND is prod, a body that schedules a notebook is refused with `ok: false` at 200 ("In production a notebook comes from Git. Deploy it with a bundle.") unless it carries a bundle deploy stamp (provenance, or one already on the pipeline); other stages and statement schedules are unaffected. A cluster or notebook store that does not answer is 502 or 503 as on create. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

| `viewers` | array of string (nullable) | No |  | Groups that may read the pipeline without being members (`spec.viewers`). At most 16, each a group name; omitted writes none. A bundle's pipeline file carries it. |  |

**Responses**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | The verdict: accepted (with the action) or the reason it is not |
| `401` | No token to sign in with |
| `502` | The cluster did not answer |
| `503` | No cluster connection |
